jobs.title: Director, Sr. Talent Development
jobs.description:
Keystone is a premier economics, technology, and strategy consulting firm built to help companies lead through transformation. As breakthrough innovations reshape industries, redefine competition and change our society, complex and highly competitive ecosystems emerge. Keystone advises technology leaders, Fortune 100 companies, their legal counsel, and governments on business, economic, litigation, and regulatory strategy in relation to these innovations and competitive eco-systems. We operate globally from offices in New York City, Boston, San Francisco, Seattle, London, Dubai, and Washington, D.C.

About the Role

The Performance Culture Center of Excellence (CoE) exists to cultivate a culture of high performance across Keystone — through a rigorous approach to assessing and developing talent, delivering clear feedback, and identifying career paths that reward performance and align individual contribution with firm goals. As we build out the CoE, we're adding to the team and looking for a Talent Development Lead to help stand up and run core programs for Keystone's senior population.

This is a hybrid role with a minimum in office requirement of 3 days per week.

We are not able to provide relocation support for this position. We value talent from all backgrounds; however, for this position, we are unable to sponsor employment visas. We welcome applications from individuals who are already authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.

Key Responsibilities

Performance & Calibration

- Drive the execution of performance evaluation and talent review processes for Keystone’s senior team members, ensuring rigor, consistency, fairness, and appropriate differentiation across practices and offices.

- Maintain a continuous pulse on senior talent, with an ongoing understanding of each leader's performance, development priorities, career trajectory, and readiness for expanded responsibility or partnership.

- Design and facilitate senior talent reviews and calibration discussions, bringing together performance, team leadership, commercial contribution, and firm-building perspectives to support well-grounded decisions.

- Serve as a strategic partner to senior leaders in addressing performance challenges, role-fit questions, and readiness gaps, ensuring concerns are identified early, expectations are clear, and decisions align with the firm's performance philosophy and standards.

- Partner closely with HR on sensitive performance and transition matters, ensuring appropriate coordination, documentation, and handoffs.

Leadership Expectations & Competency Frameworks

- Maintain and continuously refine competency models, leadership expectations, scorecards, and promotion or hiring criteria for Principals, Partners, and other senior roles.

- Translate performance and competency information into actionable insights that inform promotion, role progression, leadership appointments, succession, and development decisions.

Leadership Development, Succession & Career Planning

- Guide individualized development planning, coaching, sponsorship, and stretch opportunities that accelerate leadership growth and prepare high performing talent for broader roles.

- Lead succession and leadership-pipeline planning, identifying critical roles, bench strength, future-partner candidates, readiness gaps, and targeted actions to strengthen the firm's leadership capacity.

- Support thoughtful career and role planning for senior talent, including evolving leadership mandates, internal mobility, and transitions when appropriate.

Senior Leader Enablement

- Equip Partners and other senior leaders to deliver candid, actionable, and development-oriented feedback to senior colleagues.

- Provide leaders with the tools, data, and guidance needed to assess performance and potential, sponsor future leaders, and make high-quality talent decisions.

- Identify common leadership capability gaps and recommend targeted development, coaching, or organizational interventions.

Reporting & Talent Insights

- Analyze senior talent performance, promotion, succession, retention, engagement, leadership pipeline, and development data to identify trends, risks, and recommended actions.

- Support executive decision-making through analyses, dashboards, and executive-ready reporting that provide visibility into bench strength, future-partner readiness, succession coverage, and organizational health.

- Partner closely with firm leadership, Practice Leaders, Learning & Development, HR, Talent Acquisition, and Staffing to deliver integrated senior talent solutions.

- Help drive continuous improvement by identifying opportunities to strengthen governance, simplify processes, improve the leader experience, and increase program effectiveness.

What You'll Bring

- Passion for developing exceptional leaders and building a strong, sustainable leadership bench.

- Significant consulting and relationship-management skill, with the credibility and presence to advise Partners and influence senior stakeholders without direct authority.

- Exceptional judgment and discretion when handling highly confidential, sensitive, and consequential talent matters.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to synthesize nuanced, sometimes conflicting inputs into clear recommendations.

- Analytical mindset with experience interpreting talent, performance, and succession data and translating insights into action.

- Highly organized with strong project management skills and the ability to manage multiple high-stakes processes and stakeholder groups simultaneously.

- Comfortable navigating ambiguity, constructive tension, and complex decision environments while building new programs and operating models.

- Service-oriented mindset and the ability to build trusted relationships with senior leaders while maintaining independence and consistent standards.

- Continuous improvement orientation with a bias toward simplifying processes and scaling best practices.

In addition to annual salary, we provide an annual discretionary bonus, 401k contribution, and competitive benefits package. Actual Compensation within the range will depend upon the level the individual is hired into based on their skills, experience, and qualifications.

Annual Salary Range
$140,000 — $200,000 USD

At Keystone we believe diversity matters. At every level of our firm, we seek to advance and promote diversity, foster an inclusive culture, and ensure our colleagues have a deep sense of respect and belonging. If you are interested in growing your career with colleagues from varied backgrounds and cultures, consider Keystone.

jobs.title: Learning & Development Specialist
jobs.description:
Keystone is a premier economics, technology, and strategy consulting firm built to help companies lead through transformation. As breakthrough innovations reshape industries, redefine competition and change our society, complex and highly competitive ecosystems emerge. Keystone advises technology leaders, Fortune 100 companies, their legal counsel, and governments on business, economic, litigation, and regulatory strategy in relation to these innovations and competitive eco-systems. We operate globally from offices in New York City, Boston, San Francisco, Seattle, London, Dubai, and Washington, D.C.

About the Role

The Learning & Development team helps Keystone employees understand what great performance looks like, build the skills to do their best work, and grow meaningful careers at the firm. We are looking for a highly motivated, resourceful Senior Associate to provide broad-based support across both Learning & Development and Performance initiatives. This is a hands-on role for someone who thrives on variety, moves quickly from idea to execution, and takes pride in making complex programs run smoothly. The Senior Associate will help deliver Keystone University training, orientation and onboarding, performance programs, communications, project management, and measurement and evaluation—while stepping in wherever needed to help the team meet its commitments.

This is a hybrid role with a minimum in office requirement of 3 days per week.

We are not able to provide relocation support for this position. We value talent from all backgrounds; however, for this position, we are unable to sponsor employment visas. We welcome applications from individuals who are already authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.

Key Responsibilities

Program Delivery & Project Management

- Coordinate multiple Performance and Learning & Development initiatives from planning through execution, maintaining clear workplans, timelines, owners, dependencies, and follow-up actions.

- Provide hands-on logistical and operational support for live, virtual, and hybrid programs, including scheduling, enrollment, materials, facilitator preparation, technology, and post-program follow-up.

- Create repeatable processes, templates, trackers, and resources that improve quality, reduce administrative burden, and allow programs to scale.

Orientation & Onboarding

- Help lead the planning and delivery of new-hire orientation and onboarding, creating a welcoming, engaged experience and ensuring new employees receive the information, connections, and support they need to ramp up quickly.

- Coordinate onboarding logistics across new hire profiles and offices, partnering with Talent Acquisition, HR, IT, Office Managers and other stakeholders to ensure a cohesive employee experience.

- Maintain and improve onboarding and learning content, resources, facilitator materials, and program documentation so information remains accurate, current, and easy to use.

Performance Culture Support

- Support the execution of Keystone’s biannual performance review process through disciplined coordination, data management, communications, and follow-through.

- Maintain accurate trackers and records, monitor deadlines and completion, and proactively follow up with employees, managers, and leaders to keep processes on track.

- Help develop practical tools, templates, FAQs, and guidance that make performance and development expectations easier for employees and managers to understand and apply.

Communications & Stakeholder Coordination

- Draft clear, polished, audience-appropriate communications across email, Slack, presentations, guides, and other channels.

- Serve as a responsive, service-oriented point of contact for program questions, resolving issues directly where possible and escalating thoughtfully when needed.

- Coordinate closely with HR, Talent Acquisitions, Staffing, Facilities & Administration, IT, business leaders, subject-matter experts, and external partners to move shared work forward.

Measurement, Evaluation & Continuous Improvement

- Collect and maintain high-quality program data, including participation, completion, feedback, assessment results, and other measures of reach and effectiveness.

- Analyze quantitative and qualitative feedback, identify themes, and translate findings into concise summaries and actionable recommendations.

- Develop dashboards, reports, and executive-ready materials that communicate progress, outcomes, risks, and opportunities for improvement.

- Continuously look for ways to improve the employee experience, strengthen adoption, streamline delivery, and increase the impact of Performance Culture and Learning & Development programs.

What You'll Bring

- 2+ years of relevant professional experience in talent, learning and development, HR, program management, consulting, operations, communications, or a related field.

- A highly proactive, resourceful, and energetic working style—you see what needs to be done, take initiative, and reliably carry work across the finish line.

- Strong project management and organizational skills, with exceptional attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and stakeholders simultaneously.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the judgment to tailor messages for different audiences and levels of the organization.

- Confidence working with data, spreadsheets, surveys, and reporting, along with the ability to turn information into clear insights and recommendations.

- Strong relationship-management and customer-service skills, with a collaborative, low-ego approach and a willingness to pitch in wherever needed.

- Comfort operating in a fast-paced, evolving environment where priorities can shift and not every process is fully built.

- Sound judgment and discretion when handling confidential employee, performance, and business information.

- A continuous improvement mindset, intellectual curiosity, and genuine enthusiasm for helping people learn, perform, and grow.

In addition to annual salary, we provide an annual discretionary bonus, 401k contribution, and competitive benefits package. Actual Compensation within the range will depend upon the level the individual is hired into based on their skills, experience, and qualifications.

Annual Salary Range
$75,000 — $100,000 USD

At Keystone we believe diversity matters. At every level of our firm, we seek to advance and promote diversity, foster an inclusive culture, and ensure our colleagues have a deep sense of respect and belonging. If you are interested in growing your career with colleagues from varied backgrounds and cultures, consider Keystone.

jobs.title: MBA Consultant
jobs.location: Boston, New York City, San Francisco, Seattle, Washington D.C.
jobs.description:
Keystone is a premier economics, technology, and strategy consulting firm built to help companies lead through transformation. As breakthrough innovations reshape industries, redefine competition and change our society, complex and highly competitive ecosystems emerge. Keystone advises technology leaders, Fortune 100 companies, their legal counsel, and governments on business, economic, litigation, and regulatory strategy in relation to these innovations and competitive eco-systems. We operate globally from offices in New York City, Boston, San Francisco, Seattle, London, Dubai, and Washington, D.C.

About The Role

As an MBA Consultant, you are a versatile strategist who will own analytical workstreams, adapt quickly across problem types, and synthesize insights for high-stakes decision-making.  Keystone teams are interdisciplinary, and you will work across a wide range of problems and practice areas.

During the interview process, we assess your ability to apply your core skillset to unfamiliar questions and operate effectively outside your primary area of focus.

Final levelling is determined by education, prior experience, and interview performance.

Key Responsibilities

Data Analysis

- Own and structure end-to-end analytical workstreams, translating ambiguous business or economic questions into rigorous, testable analytical approaches.

- Design and implement advanced quantitative and  econometric  analyses (e.g., regression, causal inference, forecasting, or simulation models) using Python, R, or Stata.

- Independently assess data quality, define methodologies, and select appropriate modeling approaches, making trade-offs under uncertainty.

- Interpret results in a business /economic  context, drawing out implications, risks, and limitations—not just reporting outputs.

- Guide and review Associate-level work, ensuring analytical rigor, efficiency, and quality of execution.

Research

- Lead targeted research efforts to inform problem framing, hypothesis development, and analytical design, not just support it.

- Synthesize economic theory, industry dynamics, and technical constraints into structured hypotheses and analytical plans.

- Critically evaluate sources (academic, regulatory, market data) and determine what materially impacts the case or client decision.

- Connect qualitative insights with quantitative findings to refine direction and challenge initial assumptions.

Report Writing

- Drive development of clear, structured narratives that link analysis to actionable insights and recommendations.

- Translate complex analytical outputs into persuasive, client-ready materials, tailoring messaging to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

- Own significant sections of client deliverables (reports, memos, presentations), ensuring clarity, logical flow, and defensibility.

- Communicate findings and implications in internal and client discussions, contributing to decision-making and shaping team direction.

- Develop high-impact exhibits that convey both analytical rigor and strategic insight.

What You’ll Bring

For this particular role, an MBA is required, along with:

Education & Experience

- Bachelor’s degree in Economics, Econometrics, Finance, Mathematics or a closely related field from a top university (target GPA 3.7+).

- MBA required; Master’s degree in Analytics, Data Science, Economics, or a related field a plus.

- 5+ years of relevant experience in consulting,  product management,  data science , or strategy-oriented roles.

- Demonstrated experience owning discrete projects or workstreams, not just contributing to them.

- Exposure to strategy consulting, economic consulting, investment banking, private equity, or data/technology-driven environments.

- Evidence of academic or leadership excellence (e.g., honors, Dean’s List, leadership roles).

Analytical Skills

- Strong quantitative and problem-solving skills, with ability to independently structure analytical approaches.

- Proficiency in Python, R, or Stata, with experience working with large, complex datasets.

- Ability to translate ambiguous questions into structured analyses and actionable insights.

- Solid business and economic intuition

Communication & Mindset

- Clear, structured communicator with ability to connect analysis to business/economic implications.

- Comfort operating in ambiguity and driving workstreams forward with limited guidance.

- Experience mentoring or guiding junior team members and reviewing work for quality.

- Strong ownership mindset with bias toward action and accountability for outcomes.

- Coachable, growth-oriented, and motivated to develop toward Engagement Manager trajectory.

- Clear interest in litigation consulting and Keystone’s problem space .

In addition to annual salary, we provide an annual discretionary bonus, 401k contribution, and competitive benefits package. Actual Compensation within the range will depend upon the level the individual is hired into based on their skills, experience, and qualifications.

Annual Salary Range
$140,000 — $198,000 USD

At Keystone we believe diversity matters. At every level of our firm, we seek to advance and promote diversity, foster an inclusive culture, and ensure our colleagues have a deep sense of respect and belonging. If you are interested in growing your career with colleagues from varied backgrounds and cultures, consider Keystone.

jobs.title: Staffing Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Keystone is a premier economics, technology, and strategy consulting firm built to help companies lead through transformation. As breakthrough innovations reshape industries, redefine competition and change our society, complex and highly competitive ecosystems emerge. Keystone advises technology leaders, Fortune 100 companies, their legal counsel, and governments on business, economic, litigation, and regulatory strategy in relation to these innovations and competitive eco-systems. We operate globally from offices in New York City, Boston, San Francisco, Seattle, London, Dubai, and Washington, D.C.

We’re growing quickly and looking for a Staffing Operations Manager to support the operational and strategic success of our Staffing & Workforce Deployment function.

About the Staffing Operations Manager Role

The Staffing Operations Manager oversees the firm's Staffing & Workforce Deployment function — reviewing and validating deployment decisions, resolving complex or contested staffing requests, and setting the strategic direction for how talent flows across the firm. Day-to-day staffing decisions and execution sit with the Staffing & Workforce Associate; the Manager's role is to review those decisions, navigate difficult calls, and communicate clearly with practice leadership when situations require escalation. Beyond oversight, the Manager leads the function's longer-horizon work: staffing technology evaluation and implementation, the firm's talent skills database, staffing analytics, utilization reporting, and monthly project balancing.

This is a hybrid role with a minimum in office requirement of 3 days per week.

We are not able to provide relocation support for this position. We value talent from all backgrounds; however, for this position, we are unable to sponsor employment visas. We welcome applications from individuals who are already authorized to work in the United Kingdom without sponsorship.

Key Responsibilities:

Decision Review & Complex Request Resolution

- Review staffing placement decisions made by the Associate and approve, redirect, or escalate as appropriate

- Resolve contested or complex staffing requests — cross-practice conflicts, competing priorities, specialized skill requirements

- Navigate decision path and communication with practice leadership on difficult or sensitive staffing calls

- Own the federated staffing governance model — the process by which requests escalate from CoE-level to the central function

Staffing Analytics & Utilization

- Drive and report on staffing analytics for RevOps and firm leadership — utilization, bench time, deployment patterns, CoE-level variances

- Raise utilization concerns proactively to RevOps leadership with recommended corrective actions

- Own monthly project balancing across the firm — ensuring equitable and optimal deployment firmwide

In-Month Pacing & Demand Management

- Monitor pacing by engagement throughout the month, tracking utilization against the staffed plan and identifying staffing deviation

- Assess whether each engagement is trending to meet the month's demand target; escalate pacing risks proactively to RevOps leadership

- Report pacing status by engagement, CoE, and geography on a regular cadence

Cross-Functional Partnerships

The Staffing Operations Manager works across multiple functions to ensure staffing decisions connect to the firm's financial, operational, and talent infrastructure.

- Pipeline & Revenue Intelligence — Receive demand forecasts and pipeline signals and translate into near-term staffing projections and deployment plans; coordinate proactively when Revenue Intelligence surfaces demand cliffs, engagement extensions, or pipeline acceleration; feed in-month pacing data back to Revenue Intelligence to inform revenue forecast updates and flag where utilization deviation is creating revenue risk

- Billing Operations — Surface staffing deviation and pacing gaps when utilization shortfalls create at-risk billing; coordinate on redeployment scenarios where overpacing creates uncaptured demand that can be converted to billable revenue; flag headcount changes — additions, rolloffs, redeployments — that affect the active invoicing pipeline

- FP&A — Provide utilization, headcount, and capacity data that feeds financial planning models and period reporting; surface bench time and overallocation patterns that affect margin; own staffing input into firmwide headcount planning; coordinate on capacity cost assumptions during annual planning

- HR & Recruiting — Raise hiring signals when staffing analytics reveal persistent capacity shortfalls or skill gaps that cannot be addressed through redeployment; provide demand-driven headcount projections to inform Recruiting's pipeline planning and sourcing timelines; coordinate on onboarding logistics to ensure new hires are deployment-ready from Day 1; partner on the talent skills database to ensure Recruiting understands what profiles the firm needs as it scales

Technology & Skills Infrastructure

- Lead evaluation and selection of staffing technology / resource management application for the firm

- Own implementation and adoption of the chosen staffing platform in partnership with IT and practice leadership

- Lead build-out of the firm's talent skills database in partnership with L&D and the Product team

- Ensure the skills database is maintained, adopted, and integrated into staffing decisions over time

Process, Policy & Workforce Planning

- Own staffing policies, processes, and governance documentation; maintain and improve as the firm scales

- Own staffing input into firmwide headcount planning

Team Management

- Manage and develop the team

- Build the team's capability as the firm expands

- Ensure Associate has the tools, context, and decision frameworks to execute day-to-day staffing confidently

What Success Looks Like

- Complex staffing decisions are resolved quickly and communicated clearly — practice leaders are never left waiting

- Utilization data is visible, accurate, and acted on before variances become margin problems

- A staffing platform and skills database are selected, implemented, and adopted firmwide

- The Associate operates with confidence and autonomy on day-to-day placements; the Manager's time is spent on the harder problems

What You’ll Bring

Enthusiastic, team-player who is willing to dive in head-first in a fast-paced environment at a growing firm

- 5–7 years of experience in resource management, workforce planning, or staffing operations, preferably within professional services or consulting

- Strong analytical skills; comfortable driving staffing analytics and presenting findings to senior and executive leadership

- Experience evaluating or implementing resource management technology; familiarity with Salesforce and CRM platforms preferred

- Proficient in Microsoft Office suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook)

- Excellent judgment on complex staffing decisions; able to navigate ambiguity, competing priorities, and sensitive situations with discretion

- High professional and ethical standards; experienced handling confidential information appropriately

- Natural collaborator and people-person; able to work effectively with practice leaders, HR, Finance, L&D, and executive leadership

- Able to work independently and provide guidance to senior stakeholders across operational areas

- Organized, deadline-oriented, and comfortable managing ad hoc projects as business needs emerge

- Enthusiastic self-starter who thrives in a fast-paced, growing environment
